option_a: Both true but (R) not correct explanation / दोनों सही, (R) व्याख्या नहीं
option_b: Both (A) and (R) are false / दोनों गलत
option_c: (A) is true, but (R) is false / (A) सही, (R) गलत
option_d: Both true and (R) is correct explanation / दोनों सही, (R) सही व्याख्या
explanation: Both true; water conservation explains leaf-shedding.

question: What do we call the streams of water flowing constantly on the ocean surface in definite directions? / निश्चित दिशा में महासागरीय सतह पर बहने वाली जल की धाराओं को क्या कहते हैं?
explanation: Ocean currents flow constantly in definite directions.

question: What causes the formation of mushroom rocks? / छत्रक शैल का निर्माण किन कारणों से होता है?
explanation: Wind erosion in deserts forms mushroom rocks.

question: Consider pairs (Type of forest–Tree found) and identify how many are correctly matched: A. Tropical Rain Forest–Mahogany; B. Tropical Deciduous Forest–Rosewood; C. Thorny Bushes–Deodar; D. Mangrove Forests–Sundari. / कितने युग्म सही सुमेलित हैं?
explanation: Only Rain Forest–Mahogany and Mangrove–Sundari correct (two).

question: Which statements are correct about meteoroids? A. Found between orbits of Mars and Jupiter. B. Believed to be parts of a planet which exploded. C. Small pieces of rocks moving around the Sun, sometimes close to Earth. / उल्कापिंडों के बारे में सही कथन
option_d: Only A and C / केवल A तथा C
explanation: Only C correctly describes meteoroids.

question: A population pyramid narrow at the base and higher in size reflects: A. High death rates of infants. B. Low birth rates. C. Increased life expectancy. D. Decreased death rates. / संकरे आधार और ऊंचाई वाला जनसंख्या पिरामिड दर्शाता है:
option_a: Only A, B and C / केवल A, B और C
option_b: Only A, C and D / केवल A, C और D
option_c: Only B, C and D / केवल B, C और D
option_d: Only A and B / केवल A और B
explanation: Narrow base: low birth, high life expectancy, low death rates.

question: Agriculture includes ______. A. Growing vegetables B. Pisciculture C. Horticulture D. Rearing of livestock / कृषि में शामिल हैं ______।
option_a: Only A, C and D / केवल A, C, D
option_b: Only A and B / केवल A और B
option_d: Only A, B and C / केवल A, B और C
explanation: Agriculture includes vegetables, horticulture, livestock rearing.

question: Assertion (A): Wet clothes take a longer time to dry on a humid day. Reason (R): The rate of evaporation increases on a humid day. / अभिकथन-कारण प्रश्न
option_a: Both true and (R) is correct explanation / दोनों सही, (R) सही व्याख्या
option_b: Both (A) and (R) are false / दोनों गलत
option_c: Both true but (R) not correct explanation / दोनों सही, (R) व्याख्या नहीं
option_d: (A) is true, but (R) is false / (A) सही, (R) गलत
explanation: A true; evaporation decreases (not increases) on humid day.

question: Consider statements about migration: A. Migration has no effect on population size as equal numbers emigrate and immigrate. B. International migration is largely from less developed to more developed nations. C. Sudan is an example of a country experiencing loss in population due to emigration. / प्रवास के बारे में कथन
option_a: Only A and C are correct / केवल A और C सही
option_b: Only A and B are correct / केवल A और B सही
option_c: All A, B and C are correct / A, B और C सभी सही
option_d: Only B and C are correct / केवल B और C सही
explanation: Only B and C correct; A is false about population size.

question: Central Government offices in India open at 09:00 a.m. IST. What is the local time of opening at 78°30' E near Hyderabad and 92°45' E near Aizawl, respectively? / हैदराबाद और आइजोल के स्थानीय समय क्रमशः?
explanation: Hyderabad 08:44, Aizawl 09:41 relative to IST meridian.

question: Assertion (A): Polar easterlies in the northern hemisphere move towards the right direction. Reason (R): The Earth rotating on its axis affects the direction of the winds. / अभिकथन-कारण प्रश्न
option_a: Both true and (R) is correct explanation / दोनों सही, (R) सही व्याख्या
option_b: (A) is true, but (R) is false / (A) सही, (R) गलत
option_c: Both (A) and (R) are false / दोनों गलत
option_d: Both true but (R) not correct explanation / दोनों सही, (R) व्याख्या नहीं
explanation: Both true; Earth's rotation (Coriolis) explains wind deflection.

question: Which statement is true about heat zones of the Earth? / पृथ्वी के ताप कटिबंधों के बारे में कौन-सा कथन सही है?
option_a: All areas between Equator and Arctic Circle are temperate zone / विषुवत व आर्कटिक वृत्त के बीच सारा क्षेत्र शीतोष्ण
option_b: Mid-day Sun never shines overhead beyond Tropic of Cancer and Capricorn / कर्क-मकर रेखा के परे दोपहर का सूर्य कभी सिर पर नहीं
option_c: In whole Southern hemisphere Sun does not rise much above horizon / पूरे दक्षिणी गोलार्द्ध में सूर्य ऊपर नहीं आता
option_d: Mid-day Sun exactly overhead at least once a year on all latitudes between Cancer and Arctic Circle / कर्क व आर्कटिक के बीच सभी अक्षांशों पर
explanation: Mid-day Sun never overhead beyond the two tropics.

question: Which statements are correct for temperate zones? A. Temperate zones have moderate temperature. B. Mid-day Sun never shines overhead on any latitude in this zone. C. It spans between the Arctic Circle and the Equator in the Northern hemisphere only. / शीतोष्ण कटिबंध के लिए सही कथन
option_a: Only A and B / केवल A और B
option_b: Only A and C / केवल A और C
option_d: All A, B and C / A, B और C सभी
explanation: Temperate: moderate temperature, Sun never overhead (A and B).

question: In which state would you find the sea coast where Vasco da Gama first landed after discovering the sea route from Europe to India? / वास्को डी गामा पहली बार किस राज्य के तट पर पहुंचे थे?
explanation: Vasco da Gama landed at Kozhikode (Calicut), Kerala, 1498.

question: 'An African-American refused to give up her seat on a bus to a white man in 1955 and the incident led to the Civil Rights Movement in USA.' Who was this person? / यह व्यक्ति कौन थी?
explanation: Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat in 1955.

question: The most distinctive aspect about tribal societies is that there is very little ______ among them. / आदिवासी समाजों का अति विशिष्ट पहलू यह है कि उनके बीच बहुत ही कम ______ है।
explanation: Tribal societies have very little hierarchy among members.

question: Consider statements: (A) Enforcement of laws is even more important when the law seeks to protect the weak from the strong. (B) Markets everywhere tend to be exploitative of workers only. / कथनों पर विचार कीजिए
option_c: Both (A) and (B) are correct / दोनों सही
option_d: Neither (A) nor (B) is correct / न (A) न (B)
explanation: Only A correct; markets exploit beyond just workers.

question: The National Medical Commission's Code of Medical Ethics states every physician should prescribe drugs that come under ______ medicines. / राष्ट्रीय चिकित्सा आयोग की आचार-संहिता में हर चिकित्सक को ______ दवाएं लिखनी चाहिए।
explanation: Physicians should prescribe generic medicines per NMC code.

question: What would you commonly associate a ginning mill with? / एक जिनिंग मिल को आप किसके साथ जोड़ेंगे?
explanation: A ginning mill separates cotton from seeds into bales.

question: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) are being used in India since 2004 for all general elections. It mainly saves ______. / भारत में 2004 से EVM का उपयोग मुख्यतः ______ बचाती है।
option_a: Approximately 1,50,000 trees required for ballot papers / लगभग 1,50,000 पेड़
option_b: The energy and efforts of local public / स्थानीय जनता की ऊर्जा
option_c: The time of voters and the Election Commission / मतदाताओं व आयोग का समय
option_d: The money transferred illegally for votes / अवैध धन हस्तांतरण
explanation: EVMs mainly save ~1,50,000 trees used for ballot papers.

question: Which mechanism in a democratic country puts a limit on the powers of the government? / एक लोकतांत्रिक देश में कौन-सी कार्यविधि सरकार की शक्तियों पर नियंत्रण लगाती है?
option_a: Presence of pressure groups / दबाव-गुटों की उपस्थिति
option_d: People asserting their rights / अधिकारों का दावा करने वाली जनता
explanation: Regular elections limit the government's powers.

question: Which statements are true? A. 'Women are emotional' is a common gender stereotype. B. Concepts of purity and pollution are associated with caste system. C. 'English is a superior language' is a prejudiced statement. D. Recognition of plurality of religions is not a feature of diversity in India. / कौन-से कथन सही हैं?
option_a: Only B and D / केवल B और D
option_b: A, B and C / A, B और C
explanation: A, B, C true; D false—religious plurality is a feature.

question: A stereotypical viewpoint regards housework as ______. / एक रूढ़िबद्ध धारणा के अनुसार घरेलू काम ______ होते हैं।
option_a: Women's natural work / महिलाओं के लिए स्वाभाविक काम
option_b: Time-consuming for women / महिलाओं का समय लेने वाले काम
option_c: Difficult for women / महिलाओं के लिए मुश्किल काम
option_d: Valuable work that women do / महिलाओं द्वारा किए गए मूल्यवान काम
explanation: Stereotype: housework as women's natural work.

question: Which of the following are features of the Indian Constitution? A. Special privileges for supremacy of judiciary. B. Adopts universal adult franchise. C. Guarantees equality before law to all citizens. D. Special privileges to the poorest and most disadvantaged Indians. / भारतीय संविधान की विशेषताएं
option_a: A, B and C only / केवल A, B तथा C
option_b: A, B and D only / केवल A, B तथा D
option_c: B, C and D only / केवल B, C तथा D
option_d: A, C and D only / केवल A, C तथा D
explanation: B, C, D are features; A (judiciary supremacy) is not.

question: Which Fundamental Rights are given to every arrested person under Article 22? A. Right to be informed of the offence. B. Right to be presented before a magistrate within 48 hours. C. Right not to be ill-treated or tortured. D. Right of women and children not to be arrested. / अनुच्छेद 22 के तहत अधिकार
option_a: Only B, C and D / केवल B, C और D
option_b: Only A and D / केवल A और D
option_c: Only A and B / केवल A और B
option_d: Only A and C / केवल A और C
explanation: Article 22: right to know offence (A) and no torture (C).

question: Which part of the Indian Constitution serves as a guide to institute laws and policies that help reduce the poverty of the masses? / संविधान का कौन-सा भाग गरीबी कम करने के लिए मार्गदर्शक है?
option_c: Directive Principles of State Policy / राज्य के नीति निर्देशक सिद्धांत
explanation: DPSP guides laws and policies to reduce poverty.

question: Which statements are correct regarding evaluation? A. As per NEP 2020, evaluation will be creative and multidimensional (360 degree) holistically. B. Formative assessment is competency-based, promotes learning. C. Criterion-referenced assessment refers to how a student scores compared to other students. D. Norm-referenced assessment refers to how a student's score compares to a pre-determined standard. / मूल्यांकन के संबंध में सही कथन
option_a: A, C and D only / केवल A, C और D
option_b: A, B, C and D / केवल A, B, C और D
option_c: A and D only / केवल A और D
explanation: A and B correct; C and D definitions are swapped/wrong. (Key: B)

question: What sequence must students follow to prepare a project on 'Role of Government in Health System'? A. Presenting findings B. Deciding on objectives C. Planning collection of data D. Finding specific sources of data / परियोजना कार्य का सही क्रम
explanation: Objectives, plan data, find sources, present findings (B,C,D,A).

question: Which source provides primary information 'to teach about challenges faced by women at workplace'? / कौन-सी प्राथमिक सूचना उपलब्ध करवा सकती है?
explanation: Personal interviews are the primary source here.

question: Which methods of teaching social science involve students to go beyond textbooks? A. Project work B. Lecture C. Questioning D. Demonstration / छात्रों को पाठ्यपुस्तक के परे जाने वाली विधियां
option_a: A, B and C / A, B तथा C
option_b: A, C and D / A, C तथा D
option_c: A and B / A तथा B
option_d: B and C / B तथा C
explanation: Project work, questioning, demonstration go beyond textbooks.

question: Which questions will develop critical or logical thinking in students? A. Open-ended questions B. Closed-ended questions C. Exploratory questions D. Convergent questions / कौन-से प्रश्न आलोचनात्मक चिंतन विकसित करेंगे?
option_a: B, C and D / B, C और D
option_b: A, C and D / A, C और D
option_c: A, B and D / A, B और D
option_d: A, B and C / A, B और C
explanation: Open-ended, exploratory, convergent questions develop thinking.

question: What is the main objective of peer assessment in evaluation? / सहपाठी आकलन का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है?
option_a: Enabling students to learn to assess and provide constructive feedback / आकलन करना सीखना व रचनात्मक प्रतिपुष्टि
option_b: Making evaluation simple and easy for the teacher / शिक्षक के लिए सरल बनाना
option_c: Strengthening social relationships while giving feedback / सामाजिक संबंधों को दृढ़ करना
option_d: Providing a structured learning process to critique peers / आलोचना की संरचित प्रक्रिया
explanation: Peer assessment: learn to assess and give constructive feedback.

question: During a discussion on 'How Weather Forecasts Help Us' in a social studies class, a teacher may: / 'मौसम का पूर्वानुमान' विषय पर शिक्षक:
option_a: Show a PowerPoint containing summary of textbook contents / पाठ्यपुस्तक सारांश की प्रस्तुति दिखाए
option_b: Assign the role of persons involved in different rural and urban professions to students / विभिन्न व्यवसायों की भूमिका नियत करे
option_c: Show a news clip on weather forecasting / मौसम पूर्वानुमान की क्लिप दिखाए
option_d: Ask students to draw pictures of different weather conditions / मौसम स्थितियों के चित्र बनवाए
explanation: Assigning professional roles connects forecasts to real life.

question: While discussing gender roles in the classroom a teacher should: A. Suggest different professions for males and females. B. Offer different types of education to boys and girls. C. Lay emphasis on challenging gender stereotypes in everyday life. / जेंडर भूमिकाओं पर चर्चा करते समय
option_a: A and B / A तथा B
option_b: B and C / B तथा C
option_c: A and C / A तथा C
explanation: Teacher should only challenge gender stereotypes (C).

question: A learner is continuously getting low marks in social science. Which assessment is required to understand the difficulties? A. Placement B. Summative C. Diagnostic D. Formative / कठिनाइयों को समझने के लिए कौन-सा आकलन?
option_a: A and D / A तथा D
option_c: C and D / C तथा D
option_d: A and B / A तथा B
explanation: Diagnostic and formative assessments identify difficulties.

question: Ambika wants to teach her class about land features, ocean currents, volcanoes and climate. Which teaching-learning material should she choose? / अंबिका को कौन-सी सामग्री चुननी चाहिए?
option_a: Working models, maps, globe / कार्यकारी मॉडल, मानचित्र, ग्लोब
option_b: Charts, scrapbooks, graphs / चार्ट, स्क्रैपबुक, ग्राफ
option_c: Graphs, pictures, flashcards / ग्राफ, तस्वीरें, फ्लैश कार्ड
option_d: Timelines, blackboard, specimens / काल रेखाएं, ब्लैकबोर्ड, नमूने
explanation: Working models, maps, globe suit these geographic topics.

question: The objectives of teaching history are to: A. Illustrate sources used to reconstruct history. B. Appreciate skills and knowledge of early societies. C. Identify archaeological evidences and make deductions. D. Remember all dates, places and persons in textbooks. / इतिहास शिक्षण के उद्देश्य
option_a: B, C and D / B, C और D
option_b: A, B and D / A, B और D
option_c: A, C and D / A, C और D
option_d: A, B and C / A, B और C
explanation: History teaching: sources, early societies, archaeological deduction (A,B,C).

question: Consider statements: (A) Cooperative learning and collaborative learning are two different methods to teach social sciences. (B) In a classroom, each student prepared a presentation on 'Our Food' and contributed to the overall theme—an example of collaborative learning. / कथन A और B
option_a: Both (A) and (B) are correct / दोनों सही
option_d: Both (A) and (B) are incorrect / दोनों गलत
explanation: Both correct; cooperative and collaborative differ, example fits.

question: The teacher tells students that 'temperature decreases with increase in height up to a certain level'. Then students solve problems on temperature at different latitudes. This is an example of: / यह किसका उदाहरण है?
explanation: General rule then specific problems = deductive approach.

question: Sonu is a visually disabled student of class VII. Choose the correct option: / सोनू कक्षा VII का दृष्टिबाधित छात्र है, सही विकल्प चुनिए:
option_a: Social science teacher must modify her teaching and assessment strategies to include him in the normal class / शिक्षक अपनी विधियों में बदलाव कर सामान्य कक्षा में समावेश करे
option_b: He must be in a special school / विशेष विद्यालय में हो
option_c: All students should be sympathetic towards him / सभी सहानुभूति रखें
option_d: He can study in a normal school but promoted without examination / बिना परीक्षा पदोन्नति
explanation: Teacher must modify strategies to include him in normal class.

question: A middle school social studies teacher assigns project work on Shivaji. Which would be highly relevant to develop critical thinking? A. Prescribed textbook B. Books from school library C. Details from more than one Internet website D. Information shared by the teacher in class E. Information shared in social networking applications / शिवाजी पर परियोजना के लिए
option_a: Only A, C, D and E / केवल A, C, D और E
option_b: Only A, B and C / केवल A, B और C
option_c: Only A, B, C and D / केवल A, B, C और D
option_d: Only A and D / केवल A और D
explanation: Textbook, library books, multiple websites, teacher input (A,B,C,D).

question: Which questions/activities promote analytical thinking and creativity? A. Which river did the Harappan civilization settle near? B. Make a map of your house. C. Why are day and night not equal throughout the year? D. What is the purpose of celebrating festivals? / कौन-से प्रश्न विश्लेषणात्मक चिंतन बढ़ाते हैं?
option_a: Only A and B / केवल A और B
option_b: A, C and D only / केवल A, C और D
option_c: Only C and D / केवल C और D
option_d: Only A and D / केवल A और D
explanation: 'Why' questions (C and D) promote analytical thinking.

question: Which could be the aim of a social science teacher? A. Making students respond to desired situations. B. Accepting the student as an active learner. C. Controlling free expression to maintain discipline. D. Giving importance to ambitious behaviour, motivating them to become ambitious. / सामाजिक विज्ञान शिक्षक का उद्देश्य
option_b: A, C and D only / केवल A, C और D
option_c: A, B, C and D / A, B, C और D
explanation: Accepting student as an active learner is the aim (B).

question: Which would be the correct sequence of steps in the 5E model lesson plan? / 5E मॉडल पाठ योजना के पदों का सही क्रम?
option_a: Evaluate, explain, explore, engage, elaborate / मूल्यांकन, व्याख्या, अन्वेषण, संलग्न, विस्तार
option_b: Engage, explore, explain, elaborate, evaluate / संलग्न, अन्वेषण, व्याख्या, विस्तार, मूल्यांकन
option_c: Explore, engage, explain, elaborate, evaluate / अन्वेषण, संलग्न, व्याख्या, विस्तार, मूल्यांकन
option_d: Explain, elaborate, evaluate, engage, explore / व्याख्या, विस्तार, मूल्यांकन, संलग्न, अन्वेषण
explanation: 5E model: Engage, Explore, Explain, Elaborate, Evaluate.

question: Assertion (A): In the classroom, concepts should be explained through the lived experiences of individuals and communities. Reason (R): Teaching generalised notes on cultural, social and class differences may generate their own biases, prejudices and attitudes in classroom. / अभिकथन-कारण प्रश्न
option_a: Both true and (R) is correct explanation / दोनों सही, (R) सही व्याख्या
option_b: (A) is false, but (R) is true / (A) गलत, (R) सही
option_c: Both true but (R) not correct explanation / दोनों सही, (R) व्याख्या नहीं
option_d: (A) is true, but (R) is false / (A) सही, (R) गलत
explanation: Both true; avoiding generalisations explains lived-experience approach.

question: Assertion (A): Explaining civilization and culture, the teacher tells children that social studies is related to culture and civilization and affirms the scientific approach. Reason (R): Social science has nothing to do with art; science combined with society becomes social science; therefore related only to science. / अभिकथन-कारण प्रश्न
option_a: (A) is true, but (R) is false / (A) सही, (R) गलत
option_b: Both (A) and (R) are false / दोनों गलत
option_c: Both true but (R) not correct explanation / दोनों सही, (R) व्याख्या नहीं
option_d: Both true and (R) is correct explanation / दोनों सही, (R) सही व्याख्या
explanation: Both false; social science relates to art and humanities too.

question: Read the poem (cricket and ant fable). What did the cricket do in summer?
explanation: The silly young cricket sang through summer.

question: Study the statements: A. During winter, it was difficult to dance in the snow-covered ground. B. However, the cricket could have enjoyed skating.
option_a: A is right and B is wrong
option_b: B is right and A is wrong
option_c: Both A and B are right
option_d: Both A and B are wrong
explanation: A is right; cricket could not enjoy skating (B wrong).

question: What made the cricket go to the ant?
option_c: Piles of grains at ant's place
explanation: Starvation and famine drove the cricket to the ant.

question: Which genre does the poem belong to?
explanation: Animal characters teaching a moral make it a fable.

question: What is the theme of the poem?
option_a: We should always keep slogging like the ant.
option_b: We should always pursue our hobbies.
option_c: If we don't care for our future, we will eventually suffer.
option_d: We should keep partying and dancing.
explanation: Theme: neglecting the future leads to suffering.

question: '... sunny months of gay summer and spring.' Identify the figure of speech used in the above line.
explanation: Repeated initial sounds make it alliteration.

question: Language classroom often focuses on group and pair work. This also helps in developing an important value associated with an inclusive classroom, which is:
explanation: Group and pair work develops collaboration.

question: You bring objects to the class, ask children to name them, write responses on the blackboard, tell them these names are 'nouns' and then give its definition. The method you are using is called:
explanation: Examples to definition is the inductive method.

question: When monolingual speakers move from formal to informal modes of speech in the same spoken or gestured idea, it is called:
explanation: Shifting speech modes/registers is code-switching.

question: Some words can have more than one meaning. The meaning of words in a particular language relates to which of the following?
explanation: Word meanings in casual group usage relate to slang. (Key: D)

question: The purpose of remedial teaching is to:
option_b: Teach again, the language items not properly learnt.
option_d: Teach again, the language items already learnt.
explanation: Remedial teaching re-teaches improperly learnt items.

question: Skinner opined that children would repeat sounds if they were followed by a pleasurable response. This viewpoint has its foundation in:
explanation: Reinforced repetition of sounds reflects operant conditioning.

question: Based on your observation to develop a particular skill, you decide to use the Direct method in your class. For which skill will you use this method?
explanation: Direct method emphasizes oral communication—speaking skills.

question: Which among the following theorists hypothesized that children have a built-in readiness to learn language?
explanation: Chomsky proposed innate language acquisition (LAD).

question: To learn about the system of rules that govern how words can be meaningfully arranged to form phrases and sentences, you need to study:
explanation: Syntax studies rules for arranging words into sentences.

question: If children hear two languages spoken around them, this exposure to two languages will:
explanation: Bilingual exposure gives children a cognitive advantage.

question: Input is defined as the ______ a learner hears and responds to for its meaning.
explanation: Krashen: input is the language a learner hears for meaning.

question: Your friend is asked to teach functional grammar. You tell her that functional grammar means teaching grammar in/through:
explanation: Functional grammar teaches grammar through context.

question: A 'Recall-Type' test is a test of:
explanation: Recall-type tests assess memory.

question: Children are motivated by activities that are:
explanation: Children are motivated by activities meaningful to them.

question: You want to identify the deficiencies and difficulties of the learners in your class. Which evaluation would you use?
explanation: Diagnostic evaluation identifies learners' deficiencies.

question: Read the passage (Aimee). The doctors amputated Aimee's legs because ______.
option_b: They were not of the same length
explanation: Doctors amputated because her legs had no bones.

question: When Aimee began to use designer legs, she caught the attention of ______.
explanation: Designer legs caught the fashion and beauty industry's attention.

question: Aimee had a painful childhood because: A. Both her legs did not have bones. B. She underwent a lot of surgeries.
option_c: Both A and B are correct.
option_d: Both A and B are incorrect.
explanation: Both boneless legs and many surgeries caused painful childhood.

question: Which of the following statements is true?
option_a: The Boston meet was for double amputees only.
option_b: Aimee's mother gave her special care when she was a young child.
option_c: Soon Aimee started promoting health products.
option_d: At the Boston meet, Aimee was the only one on wooden legs.
explanation: True: Aimee was the only one on wooden legs at Boston.

question: At the Boston sports meet, Aimee discovered that all other athletes had only one artificial leg. That did not discourage her. Instead, she began to do something. What was it?
option_a: She decided to enter long jump competition next.
option_b: She decided to participate in athletics.
option_c: She decided to have designer legs.
option_d: She decided to enter the fashion industry.
explanation: She decided to enter the long jump competition next.

question: Which word is most similar in meaning to the word 'self-sufficient'?
explanation: 'Independent' is closest in meaning to self-sufficient.

question: Which word is most opposite to the word 'unconventional'?
explanation: 'Traditional' is the opposite of unconventional.

question: Identify the clause in the underlined part: 'A year later, she broke the world record in it.'
explanation: 'She broke the world record' is a principal clause.

question: Which part of speech does the underlined word belong to? 'Her mother, however, treated her as a self-sufficient person.'
explanation: 'However' functions as a conjunction here. (Key: C)

question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द भिन्न है? (गद्यांश: क्षमा)
explanation: 'दुर्बल' विशेषण है, शेष भाववाचक संज्ञाएं।

question: 'ऊंचाई प्राप्त करने का एक सशक्त माध्यम है।' इस वाक्य में 'सशक्त' एक ______ विशेषण है।
explanation: गुण दर्शाने से 'सशक्त' गुणवाचक विशेषण है।

question: क्षमा क्या नहीं है?
explanation: गद्यांश अनुसार क्षमा आत्म साधना नहीं है।

question: गंतव्य पर कौन पहुंचता है?
explanation: क्षमाशील और शांत चित्त व्यक्ति गंतव्य पर पहुंचता है।

question: धर्म का दरवाजा किसके लिए खुलता है?
option_a: क्षमा न मांगने वाले व्यक्ति के लिए
option_b: क्षमादान न करने वाले के लिए
option_c: क्षमादान का अभ्यास करने वाले के लिए
explanation: क्षमादान का अभ्यास करने वाले के लिए धर्म का दरवाजा खुलता है।

question: व्यक्तित्व का महत्वपूर्ण घटक क्या है?
explanation: क्षमा व्यक्तित्व का महत्वपूर्ण घटक है।

question: क्षमा करना कौन जानता है?
explanation: समर्थवान व्यक्ति ही क्षमा करना जानता है।

question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द भिन्न है? (गद्यांश: क्षमा सभी धर्मों का आधार)
explanation: 'संभालना' क्रिया है, शेष भाववाचक संज्ञाएं।

question: 'अक्षम लोग' में 'लोग' ______ संज्ञा है।
explanation: 'लोग' समूहवाचक संज्ञा है।

question: सामर्थ्ययुक्त, पुरुषार्थहीन और अधैर्यवान ______ शब्द हैं।
explanation: ये संज्ञा की विशेषता बताने से विशेषण शब्द हैं।

question: क्षमा मांगने से व्यक्ति का कद ______।
explanation: क्षमा मांगने से व्यक्ति का कद पहले से बढ़ जाता है।

question: वाक्य पूरा कीजिए: अहमवश अपनी गलती न मानकर ______।
option_c: क्षमा मांगने में संकोच करते हैं
explanation: अहमवश गलती न मानकर क्षमा मांगने में संकोच करते हैं।

question: ______ लोग क्षमा को कायरता कहते हैं।
explanation: पुरुषार्थहीन लोग क्षमा को कायरता कहते हैं।

question: क्षमा करने से व्यक्तित्व में क्या प्रकट नहीं होता?
explanation: क्षमा से कायरता प्रकट नहीं होती, तेजस्विता उत्पन्न होती है।

question: समय-समय पर ग्लानि की अनुभूति कब होती है?
option_a: जब हम क्षमा मांगने में संकोच करते हैं
option_b: जब हम क्षमा मांग लेते हैं
option_c: जब हम गलती स्वीकार लेते हैं
option_d: जब हम क्षमा दे देते हैं
explanation: क्षमा मांगने में संकोच करने पर ग्लानि की अनुभूति होती है।

question: एक शिक्षक होने के नाते, आप अपनी कक्षा में श्रव्य-दृश्य सामग्री और शारीरिक गतिविधियों का प्रयोग करना पसंद करते हैं। ऐसा इसलिए क्योंकि इससे:
option_a: आपको कक्षा में आराम के मौके मिल जाते हैं।
option_b: विद्यार्थियों का ध्यान दूसरी तरफ लग जाता है।
option_c: आकलन प्रभावशाली रूप से हो पाता है।
option_d: अधिगम संवर्धन हेतु इंद्रियों का अधिकतम संख्या में उपयोग होता है।
explanation: श्रव्य-दृश्य सामग्री इंद्रियों का अधिकतम उपयोग कराती है।

question: आपने अपने विद्यार्थी की उत्तर-पुस्तिका पढ़ी और उसमें टिप्पणियां लिखीं। यह किसका उदाहरण है?
explanation: उत्तर-पुस्तिका पर टिप्पणियां पृष्ठपोषण (फीडबैक) हैं।

question: अच्छे वक्ताओं के पास किस तरह की योग्यता होती है?
explanation: अच्छे वक्ता तुरंत विश्लेषण करने में सक्षम होते हैं।

question: आपकी कक्षा का एक विद्यार्थी राकेश अक्सर काल रूप की गलतियां करता है। इस समस्या से उबरने के लिए आप:
option_a: राकेश को नियम सिखाने के लिए डांट सकते हैं।
option_b: राकेश को नोटबुक में दस बार नियम लिखने को कह सकते हैं।
option_c: उसे व्याकरण के नियम समझा सकते हैं।
option_d: समूची कक्षा में कई उदाहरण प्रस्तुत कर राकेश पर ध्यान दे सकते हैं।
explanation: कई उदाहरण देकर व्यक्तिगत ध्यान देना सर्वाधिक प्रभावी है।

question: आप सर्वाधिक उपयुक्त शिक्षण सामग्री का चयन करना चाहते हैं। मही शिक्षण सामग्री के चयन के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा प्रासंगिक नहीं है?
option_a: यह जरूरी नहीं कि इसकी विशिष्ट शैक्षिक महत्ता हो।
option_c: यह कक्षा में पढ़ाए जा रहे विषय के समरूप होना चाहिए।
option_d: यह प्रयोग के संदर्भ में सरल और सादा होना चाहिए।
explanation: शैक्षिक महत्ता जरूरी न होना कथन अप्रासंगिक (गलत) है।

question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा उद्भूत साक्षरता (emergent literacy) से संबंधित नहीं है?
option_a: मुद्रित/लिखित सामग्री के प्रति समझ बनाना
explanation: 'नोट देना' उच्च शैक्षिक कौशल है, उद्भूत साक्षरता में नहीं।

question: चुनौती बाधित कुछ बच्चों ने एक नए विद्यालय में प्रवेश लिया। कौन-सी प्रतिक्रिया समावेशी शिक्षा की अवधारणा को प्रतिबिंबित करती है?
option_a: ओफ्फो! मैं ऐसे बच्चों को कैसे पढ़ा सकती हूं जो सुन ही नहीं सकते?
option_b: अरे वाह! इस तरह से बच्चों को एक-दूसरे की मदद व सहयोग करने के अच्छे अवसर मिलेंगे।
option_c: ओफ्फो! ये बच्चे कक्षा के दूसरे बच्चों के साथ कैसे घुल-मिल पाएंगे?
option_d: अरे! इन बच्चों के लिए तो एक पृथक अनुभाग होना चाहिए।
explanation: सहयोग के अवसर देखने वाली सकारात्मक प्रतिक्रिया समावेशी है।

question: आपको कक्षा में विमर्श करना बहुत अच्छा लगता है क्योंकि:
option_a: यह शिक्षार्थियों के योगदान को महत्व नहीं देता है।
option_b: यह वाक् में स्पष्टता और विशिष्टता प्रदान करता है।
option_c: यह शिक्षार्थियों को चिंतन के लिए शायद ही प्रेरित करता है।
option_d: यह आपको अध्यापक होने की सत्ता प्रदान करता है।
explanation: कक्षा-विमर्श वाक् में स्पष्टता और विशिष्टता लाता है।

question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा वाक्य वायगोत्स्की और पियाजे के सिद्धांत के मध्य महत्त्वपूर्ण अंतर पर प्रकाश डालता है?
option_a: भाषा और विचार के मध्य संबंध
option_b: अर्थ-निर्माण की प्रक्रिया में बच्चों की रचनात्मक/वस्तुपरक भूमिका
option_c: यह समझ कि बच्चे सक्रिय/निष्क्रिय रूप से शुरुआत करते हैं
option_d: यह समझना कि अधिगम एक सरल/जटिल प्रक्रिया है
explanation: भाषा और विचार के संबंध पर दोनों सिद्धांतों में मुख्य अंतर है।

question: संप्रेषण/भाषा शिक्षण में सर्वाधिक महत्त्वपूर्ण तथ्य:
option_d: व्याकरण के नियमों को कंठस्थ करना
explanation: संप्रेषणात्मक भाषा शिक्षण में 'अर्थ' सर्वाधिक महत्त्वपूर्ण है।

question: किस वक्ता में कोड-मिश्रण में संलग्न होने की सबसे अधिक संभावना होगी?
explanation: द्विभाषी बालक कोड-मिश्रण में सर्वाधिक संलग्न होता है।

question: कक्षा IV की विद्यार्थी मंदाकिनी काल के संबंध में अक्सर गलतियां करती है। आप उसकी मदद कैसे करेंगे?
option_a: उसे जीवन की वास्तविक परिस्थितियों से जुड़े उदाहरण प्रस्तुत करेंगे जिनमें वह कालों का प्रयोग कर सके
option_b: उसे कालों के नियम अच्छी तरह से कंठस्थ करने के लिए कहेंगे
option_c: व्याकरण के नियम समझाएंगे या लिखवाएंगे
option_d: मंदाकिनी को अपनी नोटबुक में दस बार काल लिखने के लिए कहेंगे
explanation: वास्तविक जीवन से जुड़े उदाहरण सबसे प्रभावी सहायता हैं।

question: एक भाषा अध्यापिका अपनी कक्षा में समस्या-समाधान विधि को प्रभावशाली तरीके से संचालित करना चाहती है। उसे क्या करना चाहिए?
option_a: विद्यार्थियों को अपने अभिभावकों से परामर्श लेने के लिए कहना चाहिए
option_b: विद्यार्थियों की गतिविधियों का दूर से ही अवलोकन करना चाहिए
option_c: अपसारी चिंतन (डाइवर्जेंट) को प्रोत्साहित करना चाहिए
option_d: प्रक्रिया में सक्रिय रूप से भाग लेना चाहिए
explanation: अपसारी चिंतन को प्रोत्साहित करना समस्या-समाधान प्रभावी बनाता है।

question: एक श्रोता एक श्रव्य सामग्री सुनते समय मुख्य विचार सुनता है, अनुमान लगाता है, निष्कर्ष निकालता है और सारांशीकरण करता है। इन युक्तियों को क्या कहा जाएगा?
explanation: पूर्व-ज्ञान से मुख्य विचार समझना टॉप-डाउन प्रक्रिया है।

question: ध्वनिग्रामिक जागरूकता किससे संबंधित है?
option_a: बोले जा रहे शब्दों में ध्वनिग्राम की पहचान और उनमें हेर-फेर की क्षमता
option_b: ध्वनिग्राम और ग्राफीम के बीच संबंध स्थापित करने की योग्यता
option_c: शब्दों को सही तरीके से और प्रवाह के साथ पढ़ना
explanation: ध्वनिग्रामिक जागरूकता ध्वनिग्राम-ग्राफीम संबंध से जुड़ी है। (Key: B)

question: Assertion (A): Students with poor writing abilities are often stereotyped by their teachers as 'intellectually disabled'. Reason (R): Teachers tend to have implicit bias and hold assumptions about students' learning behaviours that can affect students' growth. Choose the correct option.
option_a: A is true but R is false.
option_b: Both A and R are false.
option_c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_d: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
explanation: Poor writing stereotyping and teacher implicit bias; R correctly explains A.

question: Which of the following is not a way to promote diversity in the classroom?
option_a: Adapting behaviour based on stereotyping students according to their backgrounds and cultures
option_b: Providing opportunities for students to interact with individuals from different backgrounds and cultures
option_c: Incorporating a variety of perspectives and experiences in the curriculum
option_d: Encouraging students to express their unique identities and cultures
explanation: Adapting behaviour via stereotyping does not promote classroom diversity.

question: Which of the following is the correct match of learning disability and challenge caused by it?
option_a: Dyslexia–Impacts ability to learn numbers and arithmetic operations.
option_b: Dyspraxia–Impacts ability to see, hear and talk properly.
option_c: Dyscalculia–Impacts ability to read and language processing skills.
option_d: Dysgraphia–Impacts fine motor skills and spelling.
explanation: Dysgraphia impacts fine motor skills and spelling; correct match.

question: Students struggling with 'autism' show ease at
explanation: Autism students find ease in familiar, predictable routines.

question: Which of the following statements is not correct about gifted children?
option_a: Gifted children are born with extraordinary abilities and potential that need to be nurtured.
option_b: Gifted children have lower sense of curiosity and poor imagination skills.
option_c: Children can be gifted at different levels and some can have some kind of disability also.
option_d: Children can be gifted in more than one kind of intelligence.
explanation: Gifted children having low curiosity/poor imagination is not correct.

question: Error analysis by students–
option_a: Is a futile activity in process of learning.
option_b: Supports students in retaining their learning.
option_c: Creates further gaps in students' understanding.
explanation: Error analysis supports students in retaining their learning.

question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding declarative knowledge and procedural knowledge?
option_a: Procedural knowledge is generally process-oriented in nature.
option_b: Procedural Knowledge tells the factual knowledge about something.
option_c: Declarative Knowledge emphasizes how to do something.
option_d: Declarative knowledge is also known as analytical knowledge.
explanation: Procedural knowledge is process-oriented in nature; correct statement.

question: Contents which require an extension or modification of existing cognitive structures take ____ time for learning and are retained for ____ duration.
explanation: Accommodation content takes long time and is retained long.

question: Assertion (A): Teachers should encourage children to focus on questions such as "What is my learning goal and what do I need to do to get there". Reason (R): When students understand how to self-assess their work performance, they can use this understanding to help themselves learn and progress. Choose the correct option.
option_a: A is true but R is false.
option_b: Both A and R are false.
option_c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_d: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
explanation: Metacognition focus with self-assessment; R correctly explains A.

question: In guided discovery approach of learning–
option_a: Opportunities are provided to learners to construct knowledge for themselves.
option_b: Teacher acts as a dictator and learners act as listeners.
option_c: Learners are left on their own without any kind of intervention by teacher.
option_d: No prior planning or previous knowledge is required.
explanation: Guided discovery lets learners construct knowledge for themselves.

question: Which of the following strategies is not effective while developing conceptual understanding in children?
option_a: Asking students to generate their own examples
option_b: Asking students to memorize the definition as it is
option_c: Presenting a wide range of examples in diverse contexts
option_d: Presenting non-examples to show what the concept is not
explanation: Rote memorizing definitions is ineffective for conceptual understanding.

question: An active middle school classroom should be founded on the theoretical principles of
explanation: Active middle school classroom founded on social constructivism principles.

question: Assertion (A): Empathy depends on the ability to understand that others have feelings and to gauge their feelings. Reason (R): Emotions and cognition are not related to each other. Choose the correct option.
option_a: A is true but R is false.
option_b: Both A and R are false.
option_c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_d: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
explanation: Empathy assertion true; emotions-cognition unrelated claim is false.

question: A middle school teacher can enable students become strategic self-motivated learners by–
option_a: Dictating well-prepared answers to questions in the textbook.
option_b: Stressing upon objective-type testing at the end of the term.
option_c: Encouraging students to develop their metacognitive knowledge and skills.
option_d: Providing varied forms of reinforcement for every task completed.
explanation: Developing metacognitive knowledge makes students strategic self-motivated learners.

question: Which of the following exemplifies intrinsic motivation?
option_a: Motivation driven by competition with others
option_b: Motivation driven by gaining the appreciation of others
option_d: Motivation driven by personal interest or enjoyment of the task
explanation: Personal interest or enjoyment exemplifies intrinsic motivation.

question: Which debate is highlighted in the following question? "Does an individual's biologically determined sex bring with it all the characteristics that define one's socially constructed gender?"
explanation: Sex versus gender question highlights Nature-Nurture development debate.

question: A major developmental task during ____ is the search for identity—personal, sexual and occupational.
explanation: Search for identity is a major task during adolescence.

question: Assertion (A): Children learn values and norms of the society in overt as well as covert ways. Reason (R): Socialization is the simple process of passing on customs and rituals of the society. Choose the correct option.
option_a: A is true but R is false.
option_b: Both A and R are false.
option_c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_d: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
explanation: Values learned overtly/covertly true; socialization as simple process false.

question: As per Jean Piaget's theory of cognitive development, which of the following abilities distinguishes formal operational thinking from concrete operational thinking?
explanation: Abstract logic distinguishes formal from concrete operational thinking.

question: A significant critique of Jean Piaget is that he failed to adequately consider the influence of ____ on development.
explanation: Piaget critiqued for neglecting culture's influence on development.

question: Which of the following is a correctly matched pair?
option_a: Law and order orientation–Upholding principles of social justice for humanity
option_b: Social contract orientation–Consideration of perception of others
option_c: Punishment and obedience orientation–Avoidance of bad consequences
option_d: Good boy-Good girl orientation–Greatest good for greater numbers
explanation: Punishment-obedience orientation matches avoidance of bad consequences (Kohlberg).

question: Jean Piaget and Lev Vygotsky are similar in their belief that–
option_a: Culture has a profound effect on the learning.
option_b: Development of children takes place in stage-like progression.
option_c: Children are involved in the process of meaning making.
explanation: Piaget and Vygotsky both see children as meaning-makers.

question: Lev Vygotsky proposed that
option_a: Children's thinking is 'qualitatively' different from adults.
option_b: Children have a lot of potential which includes tasks they can do with the others' support.
option_c: Children are born 'unruly' and society needs to teach them social behaviours.
option_d: Children's thinking is 'quantitatively' different from adults.
explanation: Vygotsky: children's potential includes tasks done with others' support.

question: Assertion (A): The purpose of administering intelligence tests and extended observation should be to compare children in specific domains and abilities. Reason (R): Intelligence is an innate ability and cannot be nurtured. Choose the correct option.
option_a: A is true but R is false.
option_b: Both A and R are false.
option_c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_d: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
explanation: Both assertion and reason about intelligence testing are false.

question: A teacher who consciously takes examples of scientists of all genders in her middle school classroom is trying to–
explanation: Using all-gender scientist examples aims to break gender stereotypes.

question: Assertion (A): All girls are hardworking and sincere while boys are intelligent and dominating. Reason (R): Two distinctive biological brains produce all differences in physical and cognitive skills as well as personalities and temperament in girls and boys. Choose the correct option.
option_a: A is true but R is false.
option_b: Both A and R are false.
option_c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_d: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
explanation: Gender generalization and biological-brain reason both are false.

question: Individual differences in learning preferences of students should be seen as–
option_c: Abnormal parameter of their differing IQ levels.
explanation: Individual learning-preference differences are a normal depiction of diversity.

question: The kind of assessment in which a student's scores are compared with the average performance of other students is called–
explanation: Comparing scores with others' average is norm-referenced assessment.

question: Which of the following statements about classroom assessment are correct? I. Assessments should influence the students' cognitive processes while they study. II. Assessments should serve as learning experiences in themselves. III. Assessments should create fear and stress among students to get them to learn. IV. Assessments should be standardized and norm-referenced. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Assessments influencing cognition and serving as learning experiences are correct.

question: Which of the following questions would promote higher-order critical and analytical thinking skills among the students?
option_a: Read the newspaper articles and make a list of new words
option_b: Read the newspaper article and think of a suitable title
option_c: Identify the assumptions underlying two newspaper articles depicting the same event
option_d: Identify the nouns mentioned in a specific newspaper article
explanation: Identifying assumptions in two articles promotes higher-order critical thinking.

question: Which of the following is not included in the preamble of the Indian constitution?
explanation: 'Freedom' is not included in the Preamble of Indian Constitution.

question: A situation where a person does not have resources and opportunities that are available to other persons is known as
explanation: Lacking resources/opportunities others have is called inequality.

question: Which of the following is/are not characteristic/characteristics of democratic government?
option_a: Indirect participation of people in decision making
option_b: The Prime Minister has absolute power
option_c: Explain and defend its actions to the people
explanation: PM having absolute power is not a democratic government characteristic.

question: Which of the following functions does not come under the jurisdiction of Municipal corporations?
explanation: Maintaining law and order and making laws are outside municipal jurisdiction.

question: Which of the following sequences in context of market chain is correct?
explanation: Producer-Wholesaler-Retailer-Consumer is the correct market chain sequence.

question: Read the statements. Statement A: Employment guarantee programmes in rural areas can decrease migration from rural to urban areas. Statement B: One of the main reasons for rural to urban migration has been the higher income jobs available in urban areas. Choose the correct option.
option_a: Both A and B are true and B is the reason for A.
option_b: Both A and B are true but B is not the reason for A.
option_c: A is true but B is false.
option_d: A is false but B is true.
explanation: Both statements true but B is not the reason for A.

question: Match Column A (Panchayati Raj Institutions) with Column B (Tasks): (i) Gram sabha (ii) Gram Panchayat (iii) Janpad Panchayat (iv) Zila Parishad with (a) Regulating money among Gram Panchayats (b) Coordinating activities of various Panchayats (c) Approving BPL list (d) Maintaining water sources.
explanation: Correct match of Panchayati Raj institutions with their respective tasks.

question: What does 'double burden' refer to?
option_a: Women doing household chores and working outside the home too
option_b: Young girls doing household chores and looking after younger siblings too
option_c: Boys expected to be physically as well as emotionally strong
option_d: Pressure on men to get high-salaried job and not be emotionally weak
explanation: 'Double burden' means women doing housework plus working outside home.

question: The ____ protect citizens against the arbitrary and absolute exercise of power by the state.
explanation: Fundamental Rights protect citizens against arbitrary state power.

question: Which of the following acts violate Article 21 of the Constitution of India? (A) A sanitation staff not getting minimum wages (B) Private schools charging exorbitant fees (C) A textile company contaminating groundwater which is a drinking water source (D) Denying hawkers to carry trade on pavements. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Minimum wage denial and groundwater contamination violate Article 21.

question: Consider the following statements: Statement A: If an FIR has been registered for a cognizable offence, the police can detain any relative of the accused for 24 hours. Statement B: The police investigation includes collecting different kinds of evidence. Choose the correct option.
option_a: Both A and B are true and B is the reason for A.
option_b: Both A and B are true but B is not the reason for A.
option_c: A is true but B is false.
option_d: A is false but B is true.
explanation: Detaining relatives is false; police collecting evidence is true.

question: Which of the following could be an appropriate way to counter the marginalization of Adivasis?
option_a: Appeal them to adapt into the ways of living of majority community
option_c: Ask them to migrate to cities
option_d: Showcase their culture as exotic in media
explanation: Teaching Adivasi history in schools counters their marginalization appropriately.

question: Which of the following communities has/have been provided constitutional safeguards by enacting the prevention of Atrocities Act in 1989? (A) Minorities (B) Women (C) Scheduled Castes (D) Scheduled Tribes. Choose the correct option.
explanation: 1989 Atrocities Act gives safeguards to Scheduled Castes and Tribes.

question: The boundaries of disciplines that make up the social sciences need to be opened up and a plurality of approaches may be applied to understand a given phenomenon. What is this approach called?
explanation: Opening discipline boundaries with plural approaches is interdisciplinary thinking.

question: Which of the following is foundational logic in the drafting of syllabi of social science?
option_b: Epistemic shift towards patriarchal nationalist frame
explanation: Inclusion of local perception is foundational logic in social-science syllabi.

question: The concept of a 'fair trial' is an important one while talking about the criminal justice system. To teach this concept, you narrate to the students the story of a person who has been accused of theft and what happens thereafter at the police station and later in the court. What pedagogical resource have you used here?
explanation: Narrating a person's theft trial story uses case study resource.

question: Which of the following should be followed by the teacher in his/her classroom to promote meaningful learning?
option_a: Promoting the 'culture of quizzing' among the students
option_b: Giving those tasks to the students which are challenging
option_c: Giving recall-based tasks to the students
option_d: Giving easy tasks to the students
explanation: Giving challenging tasks to students promotes meaningful learning.

question: Assertion A: The study of social science helps the learners in understanding the contemporary society better. Reason R: Social Science education aims at providing students essential knowledge, skills and attitude necessary for self-development and also for becoming an effective member of the society.
option_a: A is true but R is false
option_b: A is false but R is true
option_c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_d: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
explanation: Social science aids society understanding; R correctly explains A.

question: Teaching social science is a—
explanation: Teaching social science is a professional activity requiring expertise.

question: Which of the following is/are the most suitable teaching-learning material/materials to explain different parts of the earth to the students? (A) Globe (B) Map (C) Atlas. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Map and Atlas are most suitable to explain earth's different parts.

question: Which of the following pedagogical techniques should be used by teachers for making social science enjoyable for students? (A) Organization of visits to museum (B) Celebration of Social Science week (C) Encouraging watching of night sky (D) Sharing large statistical data related to social facts. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Museum visits, social science week, night-sky watching make it enjoyable.

question: Two statements. Statement I: Meaningful learning in social science is a generative process of storage and retrieval of information. Statement II: Thinking, language (verbal or sign) and doing things are intimately intertwined. Options:
option_a: Statement I is true but statement II is false
option_b: Statement I is false but statement II is true
option_c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
option_d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
explanation: Statement I false; thinking, language and doing being intertwined is true.

question: Two statements. Statement I: In a democratic setup, centralization of power such as the 'Panchayati Raj System' has gained importance. Statement II: 'Panchayati Raj system' aims at raising the levels of participation and involvement of people.
option_a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
option_b: Statement I is false but statement II is true
option_c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
option_d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
explanation: Panchayati Raj is decentralization not centralization; aims to raise participation.

question: The 'sabhas' in the reign of Pallava, through their subcommittees, performed various works such as irrigation, road construction, maintenance of local temples, etc. Which of the following child-centred activities can be done to acquaint the students with the nuances of their functioning? A. Description of work division on the school campus B. Example of different groups created for classroom management C. Getting a real tour of the Sabhas of the reign of Pallava D. Getting a tour of the Sabhas of the reign of Pallava through audio-visual material. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Work division, classroom groups, audio-visual tour acquaint students with Sabhas.

question: To ensure that social science teaching moves away from an excessive emphasis on developmental issues to an understanding of issues related to justice and dignity, there needs to be a shift in focus from utilitarianism to ____.
explanation: Shift from utilitarianism to egalitarianism emphasizes justice and dignity.

question: Assertion A: An important aspect of social science is the possibility of having different shades or at times even diametrically opposite answers. Reason R: It is critical for a social science teacher to move away from the age-old habit of preaching on the pulpit.
option_a: A is true but R is false
option_b: A is false but R is true
option_c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_d: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
explanation: Both true, but reason does not correctly explain the assertion.

question: The use of iron in the Indian subcontinent began about 3000 years ago. What task would you give to your students to develop their understanding on such historical episodes? A. Reviewing the book 'What Happened in History' by Gordon Childe B. Meeting someone from the traditional blacksmithing community C. Visiting a factory under teacher supervision noting iron-making D. Collecting information by visiting a Megalithic site in the Deccan. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Blacksmith meeting, factory visit, Megalithic site visit develop historical understanding.

question: How will you assess the students through the 'project of wallpaper'? A. Seeing the selection of the subjects by the students B. Seeing the presentation on the subject matter C. Asking follow-up questions after the presentation D. Asking follow-up questions before the presentation. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Selection, presentation, and follow-up questions after assess wallpaper project.

question: Which of the following statements is not true about formative assessments?
option_a: They allow teachers to modify their own teaching strategies through ongoing feedback.
option_c: Formative assessments are a way for teachers to frequently check students' progress in a course.
option_d: The main objective of such tests is to make a final judgement about whether students have met the learning goals of the course.
explanation: Making final judgement is summative not formative assessment's objective.

question: Which of the following is true about testing?
option_a: It is a ground for admission only
option_b: It is not a trial of a student's qualities
option_c: It is a ground for critical examination
option_d: It is not a standard for comparison
explanation: Testing is a ground for critical examination of students.

question: Two statements. Statement I: learning is a continuous process. Statement II: Learning cannot take place outside the school premises. Options:
option_a: Statement I is true but statement II is false
option_b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
option_c: Both Statement I and statement II are true
option_d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
explanation: Learning is continuous; it can take place outside school premises.

question: Assertion A: Testing has a diagnostic function to indicate the presence or absence of a characteristic. Reason R: Testing is an event or a situation that comprises a set of questions or problems that analyze a person's quality of learning or determine his knowledge, abilities, etc.
option_a: A is true but R is false
option_b: A is false but R is true
option_c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
option_d: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
explanation: Testing has diagnostic function; R correctly explains the assertion.

question: Two statements. Statement I: In school education, paper-pencil tests are the only way of testing the learners. Statement II: During the testing in schools, values or numbers are assigned that represent that the learner has performed. Options:
option_a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
option_b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
option_c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
option_d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
explanation: Paper-pencil not only testing way; assigning values during testing true.

question: A place, where documents and manuscripts are stored and today all National and State Governments have them, to keep all their old official records and transactions, is called
explanation: Place storing documents and old official records is called archive.

question: Which of the following statements related to Tamil region is wrong?
option_a: The three ruling families were the Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas.
option_b: Each of the three chiefs had three centres of power.
option_d: Muvendar is a Tamil word meaning three chiefs used for heads of three ruling families.
explanation: Each chief having three power centres is the wrong Tamil-region statement.

question: Assertion: The relationship between the State and religion may be a bone of contention in today's Indian polity, but history presents workable solutions. Choose the appropriate reason/reasons for the above assertion. (A) Temples were often central to the economy and society (B) The town of Ramdaspur had developed around the central Gurudwara called Harmandar Sahib (C) Sufis were Muslim mystics who rejected outward religiosity and emphasized compassion (D) History is about the battles between different States and religions.
explanation: Temples, Ramdaspur, and Sufis support state-religion workable-solution assertion.

question: Unusual for the 12th century, Kalhana used a variety of sources. Unlike the writers of Prashastis, he was often critical about rulers and their practices. His sources include.
option_a: Earlier histories, eyewitness accounts and documents
option_b: Earlier histories, eyewitness accounts, documents and inscriptions
explanation: Kalhana used earlier histories, eyewitness accounts, documents and inscriptions.

question: Which of the following are true with regard to the Marathas? A. Shivaji carved out a stable kingdom with the support of powerful warrior families. B. Powerful warrior families were called 'Deshmukhs'. C. Highly mobile, peasant pastoralists were the backbone of the Maratha army. D. Highly mobile, peasant pastoralists were called 'Kunbis'. Choose the correct option.
explanation: All four statements about Shivaji, Deshmukhs, pastoralists and Kunbis are true.

question: Historical claim: "The Ahom built a large State." A. The Ahoms used firearms to build a large State. B. The Ahoms made high-quality gunpowder and cannons. C. The Ahom State depended upon forced labour. D. In 1662, the Ahoms defeated the Mughals. Choose the appropriate evidences for the above claim.
explanation: Firearms, gunpowder/cannons and forced labour evidence Ahom large-State claim.

question: State the validity of the following on peasant revolts. Assertion: Those who are oppressed do not always rise up in rebellion. They do so only at times. Reason: In 1859, the Indigo Ryots felt that they had the support of the local Zamindars against the planters. Conclusion: Women turned up to fight with pots, pans and kitchen implements.
option_a: Only Reason and Conclusion are valid
option_b: Only Assertion and Conclusion are valid
option_c: Assertion, Reason and Conclusion all are valid
option_d: Only Assertion and Reason are valid
explanation: Assertion, reason and conclusion on indigo peasant revolt all valid.

question: The following are some facts related to Company policies during the second half of the 18th century: A. Artisans started deserting villages. B. The company purchased goods in India by gold and silver. C. The revenue collected in Bengal could finance the purchase of goods. D. The company became the Diwan. Arrange them in sequence of their occurrence.
explanation: Correct sequence: purchased by gold, Diwan, Bengal revenue, artisans deserting.

question: Which of the following institutional developments was/were direct outcome/outcomes of the Wood's Despatch? A. Education departments of the government were set up in provinces. B. Centralization of education under the Governor General took place. C. Steps were taken to establish a system of university education. D. Indian Civil Service colleges were set up in England. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Two outcomes: provincial education departments and university education system.

question: Who amongst the following argued that before Aryan rule, there existed a golden age when warrior-Peasants tilled the land and ruled the Maratha countryside in just and fair ways?
explanation: Jyotirao Phule argued a pre-Aryan golden age of warrior-peasants.

question: Consider the following statements on Non-Brahman Movement: A. The movement came from non-Brahman castes that had acquired access to education. B. The movement argued that the Aryans were the indigenous races. C. The movement came from non-Brahman castes with wealth and influence. Choose the correct option.
option_c: Only A and C are valid
option_d: Only B and C are valid
explanation: Non-Brahman movement came from educated, wealthy, influential non-Brahman castes.

question: Social insecurities, in any society, result from a sense of alienation. In this context, the Indian Nationalist Movement was a movement: A. To acknowledge the supremacy of people over the structures of government. B. To do away with the differences of class, colour and language. C. To acknowledge the government as being equal to the God. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Nationalist movement acknowledged people's supremacy and removed class/colour/language differences.

question: It was established in Madras (Chennai) in 1864. It worked to abolish caste distinctions and promote widow remarriage and women's education. It condemned the superstitions and associated rituals of orthodox Hinduism. Identify the movement/organization.
explanation: Veda Samaj (Madras, 1864) promoted widow remarriage and women's education.

question: After the attainment of independence, why did the demand for linguistic states intensify? A. In the 1920, INC promised each linguistic group its own province. B. After independence, the congress did not take steps to honour its promise. C. The Kannada, Telugu speakers looked forward to their own state; strongest protest came from Tamil speakers of Telugu-speaking districts. D. Nehru and Patel were against the creation of linguistic States. Choose the correct option.
explanation: All options accepted by Commission for intensified linguistic-states demand.

question: In about how many days does the moon move around the earth?
explanation: The moon takes about 27 days to move around the earth.

question: Match Column-A with Column-B: (a) Tropic of cancer (b) Tropic of Capricorn (c) Arctic Circle (d) Antarctic Circle with (i) 23.5° in Southern Hemisphere (ii) 23.5° in Northern Hemisphere (iii) 66.5° South of the Equator (iv) 66.5° North of the Equator.
explanation: Tropic of Cancer 23.5°N, Capricorn 23.5°S, Arctic 66.5°N, Antarctic 66.5°S.

question: Which one of the following is not correct about the earth?
option_a: Rotation is the movement of the earth around the sun
option_b: The shape of the earth is described as a geoid
option_c: The earth is the third nearest planet to the sun
option_d: In size, the earth is the fifth largest planet
explanation: Rotation being earth's movement around the sun is not correct.

question: Read the two statements. Statement A: At any place, a watch can be adjusted to read 12 O'clock when the sun is at the highest point in the sky, i.e., when it is mid-day. Statement B: The time shown by such a watch will give the local time for that place.
option_a: A is true but B is false
option_b: A is false but B is true
option_c: Both A and B are true and B explains A
option_d: Both A and B are false
explanation: Both true; watch at solar noon shows local time, B explains A.

question: Ecosystem is formed by:
option_a: Interrelationship between organisms and their surroundings
option_d: All plants, animals and human beings
explanation: Ecosystem forms via interrelationship between organisms and their surroundings.

question: Read statements A and B. A: Human beings interact with the environment and modify it according to their need. B: A perfect balance is necessary between the natural and human environment. Choose the correct option.
option_a: A is true but B is false
option_b: A is false but B is true
option_c: Both A and B are true and B explains A
option_d: Both A and B are true but B does not explain A
explanation: Both true, but B does not explain A about environment interaction.

question: Why is tourism a major activity in ladakh-the cold desert of India? A. Visits to Gompas B. Treks to see meadows and glaciers C. Witnessing ceremonies and festivities D. It is flat plain area. Choose the correct option.
explanation: Gompa visits, treks and festivities make Ladakh tourism major; not flat.

question: Which one of the following gases is the second most plentiful gas in the air?
explanation: Oxygen (21%) is the second most plentiful gas in air.

question: Given below are four statements: A: High pressure is associated with clear sunny skies. B: Air pressure is not influenced by temperature of air. C: Low pressure is associated with cloudy skies and wet weather. D: Air always moves from high-pressure to low-pressure areas. Choose the true statements about air pressure and temperature.
explanation: High pressure clear skies, low pressure wet, air moves high to low.

question: Read statements A and B. A: Inland waterways and sea routes have been used for transport since early days. B: Waterways are the cheapest for carrying heavy and bulky goods over long distances. Choose the correct option.
option_a: A is true but B is false
option_b: A is false but B is true
option_c: Both A and B are true
option_d: Both A and B are false
explanation: Both true: waterways ancient and cheapest for heavy bulky goods.

question: Many species of plants and animals have become vulnerable or endangered and some are on the verge of extinction. Choose the reasons: (1) Afforestation (2) Landslides (3) Constructional activities (4) Poaching of animals.
explanation: Landslides, construction and poaching cause species to become endangered.

question: Read statements A and B. A: Potential resources are those resources whose entire quantity may not be known. B: These resources are not being used at present. Choose the correct option.
option_a: A is true but B is false
option_b: A is false but B is true
option_c: Both A and B are true
option_d: Both A and B are false
explanation: Both true: potential resources' quantity unknown and currently unused.

question: Match column-A with Column-B: (A) Sericulture (B) Pisciculture (C) Viticulture (D) Horticulture with (i) Growing vegetables, flowers and fruits for commercial use (ii) Cultivation of grapes (iii) Breeding of fish (iv) Commercial rearing of silkworms.
explanation: Sericulture-silkworms, Pisciculture-fish, Viticulture-grapes, Horticulture-vegetables/flowers/fruits.

question: Which poetic device is used in the expression 'Sorrowful wings'?
explanation: 'Sorrowful wings' uses the poetic device transferred epithet.

question: What is the theme of the poem?
option_a: The birds should be given good food
option_b: Birds living in the open enjoy their lives
option_c: The caged bird lives a fruitful life
option_d: The birds should be kept in a cage
explanation: The poem's theme: birds living in the open enjoy life.

question: "But my bird sings!" denotes that
option_b: My bird has regained her voice
explanation: "But my bird sings" denotes that my bird is free.

question: The speaker says that the cage-bird flutters its sorrowful wings. The wings are being described as 'sorrowful' because
option_d: The bird is sad as it is caged
explanation: Wings are 'sorrowful' because the bird is sad being caged.

question: The speaker's bird can do a number of things. It is because
explanation: The speaker's bird can do many things because it is free.

question: The caged bird is described as 'a crippled thing' because
option_d: It is not free to fly and soars
explanation: Caged bird is 'crippled' because it cannot fly and soar.

question: Which of the following statements is not true of the literary texts in language classroom?
option_a: Literary texts develop critical thinking and reflection.
option_b: Literary texts are for appreciation and enjoyment.
option_c: Literary texts should be used to teach grammar.
option_d: Literary texts are cultural inputs for language learning.
explanation: Literary texts being used to teach grammar is not true.

question: Naveen of class VI struggles with reading the text. The teacher gives him simpler text to read. She conducts shared reading sessions for him. The support provided by the teacher is called
explanation: Teacher's temporary structured reading support is called scaffolding.

question: Which approach to language teaching-learning believes 'language is a habit'?
explanation: Audiolingualism believes language is a habit built through reinforcement.

question: A child reads an unseen passage for which he is expected to answer the questions that follow. This type of reading is referred to as
explanation: Reading unseen passage to answer questions is called scanning.

question: Teacher shows five pictures to the students and asks them to write story based on these pictures. This is an example of
explanation: Writing a story from pictures is an example of creative writing.

question: Which of the following is the characteristic of performance-based assessment in language?
explanation: Contextualized communicative tasks characterize performance-based language assessment.

question: Read the following statements: A: Reading is just to understand letter-sound relationships and pronounce the words correctly. B: Reading is decoding symbols to arrive at meaning. Choose the correct option.
option_a: B is true but A is false
option_b: Both A and B are false
option_c: Both A and B are true
option_d: A is true but B is false
explanation: Reading as decoding symbols for meaning is true; A is false.

question: A teacher has to assess listening skill of her students. Which of the following activities can she select as a listening assessment?
option_a: Teacher asks the children to read a story and after that asks comprehension-based questions
option_c: Rating the children on their oral presentation
option_d: Teacher tells a story and after that asks comprehension-based questions
explanation: Telling a story then asking comprehension questions assesses listening skill.

question: ____ is concerned with the aspects of meaning in language.
explanation: Semantics is concerned with the aspects of meaning in language.

question: Which of the following is not the principle of language learning?
option_a: Language is a tool for communication
option_b: Language is learnt through memorization of structures rules of grammar
option_c: Learning a language involves mastery of both skill and knowledge
option_d: Learners may vary in their preferred approaches to learning
explanation: Learning language through memorizing grammar rules is not a principle.

question: A teacher of Grade 6 writes a word in the centre of the blackboard, and asks the learners to brainstorm all the words they can think of which are connected to the central word. The major objective of this activity is
explanation: Word-web brainstorming activity's objective is improving learners' vocabulary.

question: Assertion (A): Delaying the learning of languages in the early years makes it more difficult for children to acquire new languages. Reason (R): Early years of the child are sensitive periods for language acquisition. Choose the correct option.
option_a: A is not true but R is true
option_b: A is true but R is not true
option_c: Both A and R are true and R is a correct explanation of A
option_d: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
explanation: Delaying language learning harms acquisition; sensitive-period reason explains it.

question: One of the key principles of National Curriculum Framework for Foundational Stage (2022) with respect to multilingulalism is
option_a: Multilingualism has both cognitive and societal cultural benefits
option_b: Children must be helped to unlearn their home language and focus on school language
option_c: Multilingual nature of a classroom acts as a barrier in effective curriculum transaction
option_d: Children are not able to pick up multiple oral languages in the early years
explanation: NCF-FS 2022: multilingualism has cognitive and societal-cultural benefits.

question: In some of the speech communities, two different varieties of language coexist, each with a distinct range of social function. This situation is described as
explanation: Two coexisting language varieties by social function describe diglossia.

question: Children work in pairs. A text is divided in half. One child reads their text for the partner which the other child writes. Two of them work out the whole text. This activity is called
explanation: Paired half-text read-and-write reconstruction activity is partial dictation.

question: Which one of the following words is opposite in meaning to the word 'nominal'?
explanation: 'Substantial' is opposite in meaning to the word 'nominal'.

question: Which one of the following words is nearest in meaning to the word 'Prerequisite'?
explanation: 'Required' is nearest in meaning to the word 'prerequisite'.

question: Which part of speech is the underlined word? Japanese companies Particularly excel in this.
explanation: The underlined word 'particularly' is an adverb.

question: Identify the clause in the underlined part of the sentence: It is estimated that some 20,000 American firms have established in-house health clubs.
explanation: The underlined 'it is estimated' is a principal clause.

question: What is the prerequisite for high effect and good quality work?
option_b: Sound mind in a sound body
explanation: Sound mind in a sound body is prerequisite for quality work.

question: Japanese companies ensure loyalty and motivation by making their workers
option_c: Start off the day with exercising
explanation: Japanese companies ensure loyalty by making workers sing company song.

question: Why do companies have health clubs?
option_a: They help in better efficiency and high productivity of the workers
option_b: Health insurance companies can tie up with these health clubs
option_d: They attract profit to the company
explanation: Companies have health clubs for better efficiency and high productivity.

question: The movement towards health clubs is yet to gain momentum in India' signifies that -
option_a: Health clubs in Indian companies have not yet become popular
option_b: Due to health clubs, many consultancies have opened up
option_c: Health clubs are getting popular in Indian companies
option_d: Insurance companies are getting good premium due to health clubs
explanation: Signifies health clubs in Indian companies have not become popular.

question: What is directly affected by physical health?
explanation: Physical health directly affects the mind per the passage.

version_note: Alternative language version (Hindi) of same slot
question: नागों का गुण नहीं है
explanation: पद्यांश अनुसार घुमक्कड़ होना नागों का गुण नहीं है।

version_note: Alternative language version (Hindi) of same slot
